name: Red Lorry Yellow Lorry
label: Beggars Banquet
lede: Chris Reed built a Leeds band on a drum machine, a guitar drone and a demo tape that went out as a single untouched, then spent the next forty years insisting it was never a goth band.

hero.by: Red Lorry Yellow Lorry live, November 2004. Photo: GothEric, Wikimedia Commons

eras.title: A demo tape goes out as it is
eras.text: Leeds in the early '80s had The Sisters of Mercy, the March Violets and the Warehouse on Somers Street. Chris Reed's band came in with a guitar drone, a pounding drum machine and a love of Wire, Suicide and the MC5, and York's Red Rhino label put the demo out exactly as recorded.

years.src: Wikipedia: Red Lorry Yellow Lorry · ReGen
years.h: Chris Reed starts the band in Leeds
years.p: Reed plays guitar and writes, Mark Sweeney sings, Steve Smith plays bass and [[Mick Brown|522a231c-2133-4f6b-982b-8d38320bcd15]] drums. Sweeney is gone by the end of the year, and Reed takes the vocals for good.
years.xp:
Martin Fagan came in as second guitarist. The press filed the Lorries, as fans called them, under goth from the start; the band preferred to cite Wire and said they were mainly inspired by the MC5.

Dave Wolfenden later put the root in Suicide and the Velvet Underground: "stark, cold, confrontational."

years.src: Wikipedia: Red Lorry Yellow Lorry · Louder Than War
years.h: Red Rhino releases 'Beating My Head' straight off the demo
years.p: Manager Dave Hall hands label boss Tony K a cassette. He signs the band and puts the demo out unchanged, and it shows up strongly on the NME indie chart.

years.src: Post-Punk.com · Wikipedia: Red Lorry Yellow Lorry
years.h: Dave Wolfenden trashes his gear at his first Warehouse show
years.p: Wolfenden replaces Fagan and Paul Southern replaces Smith. Wolfenden becomes Reed's main writing partner.
years.xp:
Wolfenden says he was drunk and angry with an ex-girlfriend that night, and smashed his gear on the last song. "It wasn't planned."

He's clear about who wrote the band: "Chris was the principal songwriter and still is."

years.cap: Poster for the Belgian dates in Liege, Namur and Brussels, December 1983
years.h: John Peel books the first of two sessions
years.p: The second follows in November. They come out on CD in 2014 as BBC Sessions 1983–1984, part of Cherry Red's See the Fire.

years.cap: Red Lorry Yellow Lorry at the Richmond, Brighton, March 1984
years.src: Wikipedia: Red Lorry Yellow Lorry · Post-Punk.com
years.h: 'Monkeys on Juice' reaches No. 9 on the NME indie chart
years.p: It follows 'He's Read'. Andrew Eldritch of the Sisters of Mercy was a fan, Wolfenden says.

years.h: 'Hollow Eyes' climbs the indie singles chart to No. 7
years.p: The song later went on the debut album. Wikipedia notes good sales for a Red Rhino single.

eras.title: Two albums and the top of the indie chart
eras.text: The Red Rhino years peaked with two albums in two years. The first made No. 3 on the NME indie chart, and the second went to No. 1 on the UK independent chart. Most fans still rate the debut as the band's best.

years.cap: Red Lorry Yellow Lorry in a Red Rhino Records press photo, c. 1985
years.src: Wikipedia: Talk About the Weather · Wikipedia: Red Lorry Yellow Lorry · Trouser Press
years.h: Talk About the Weather, self-produced in Ely
years.p: Recorded at Spaceward Studio in Cambridgeshire, it stays on the NME indie albums chart for months and peaks at No. 3.
years.xp: Trouser Press heard swirling guitars and a bleak mood, and thought the album "ultimately succumbs to its own murky tunelessness, but not without a fight." Fans have tended to disagree: Wikipedia says most consider it the band's best.

years.h: 'Spinning Round', the fans' pick
years.p: A non-album single, it peaks at No. 11 on the NME indie chart. Wikipedia calls it generally felt to be the band's strongest song.

years.h: Mick Brown leaves to drum for Wayne Hussey's new band
years.p: Wayne Hussey and Craig Adams, just out of the Sisters of Mercy, decide against a drum machine and ask Brown to help. He becomes the drummer in [[The Mission|d85e95a3-07c7-4c04-a411-234290615113]].

years.src: Wikipedia: Red Lorry Yellow Lorry · Trouser Press
years.h: Paint Your Wagon goes to No. 1 on the UK indie chart
years.p: Their second album and last LP for Red Rhino, also No. 3 on the NME indie chart. Trouser Press thought it leaned too hard on [[Joy Division|9a58fda3-f4ed-4080-a3a5-f457aac9fcdd]].

years.h: For one EP, they're just the Lorries
years.p: Crawling Mantra, a four-track EP, uses the short name before the band leaves Red Rhino for Situation Two, Beggars Banquet's offshoot. Leon Phillips is now on bass.

eras.title: Beggars, RCA and a real drummer
eras.text: Situation Two brought American distribution through RCA and two albums that moved the band forward. The first was a wall of buzzing guitar; the second added live drums, keyboards and female voices. Neither charted, and Beggars let them go.

yt: Live at the Town & Country, October 1987
years.h: NME makes 'Open Up' its Single of the Week
years.p: The single, and its B-side 'The Rise', are added to the American edition of the next album.

years.h: Nothing Wrong: Situation Two in Britain, RCA in America
years.p: Bill Buchanan produces a trio record: 12 songs in under 32 minutes, ending with 52 seconds of Booker T. & the M.G.'s' 'Time Is Tight'.
years.xp:
Clips from Laurens van der Post's BBC documentary series about the Kalahari Bushmen run through the album, and stills from it make the front and back covers.

Trouser Press found it almost swamped by "an unshifting swarm of buzzing guitar noise", with 'Only Dreaming (Wide Awake)' the standout.

years.h: On Blow, a drummer replaces the machine
years.p: Mark "Chill" Chillington plays drums, and Jilly Myhill sings backing vocals. The songs are slower, with stronger melodies.
years.xp:
Wolfenden calls dropping the drum machine a controversial call at the time. Trouser Press thought Blow took "a giant step forward" and finally retired the Joy Division comparisons.

Sales disappointed, and Beggars Banquet dropped the band in 1990.

years.cap: Red Lorry Yellow Lorry promo photo, 1991
years.src: Wikipedia: Red Lorry Yellow Lorry · Discogs: Blasting Off
years.h: Blasting Off on Sparkhead, then Reed ends it
years.p: After the single 'Talking Back', the fifth album comes out on the small Sparkhead label, with Gary Weight on bass and keyboards. Reed then breaks up what's left of the band.

eras.title: Revived, then a full stop
eras.text: Reed brought the name back in 2003 with Wolfenden, toured Europe, and then went quiet for the best part of two decades. Songs worked up in weekly sessions from 2014 finally came out in 2025, on what the band said would be the last Lorries album.

years.cap: Red Lorry Yellow Lorry live, November 2004
years.h: Four new songs, download only, and a European tour
years.p: The tracks go up on the band's website. The tour's Belgian show becomes the 2005 live DVD Thunder in the Black Cave.

years.cap: Chris Reed playing solo at Leeds Poly
years.h: Reed goes acoustic as the Chris Reed Unit
years.p: The album is Minimal Animal.

years.h: Cherry Red boxes up the 1980s
years.p: Albums & Singles 1982–1989: all four albums plus singles, B-sides and remixes, 73 tracks, with a Wolfenden interview in the booklet.

years.src: ReGen · Wikipedia: Red Lorry Yellow Lorry
years.h: 'Driving Black', the first new music in almost 20 years
years.p: The Driving Black EP comes out with Simon "Ding" Archer on bass and Martin Henderson on drums.

years.big: "It's the full stop at the end."
q: There is no more un-recorded Lorries material.
years.h: Strange Kind of Paradise, announced as the last album
years.p: Released on COP International, it collects songs worked up in weekly sessions since 2014 and held up by COVID and personal circumstances, Dave Wolfenden told ReGen.
